hook.text: Early cars used gas lamps that flickered in the wind. Modern headlights see farther than you can.

buildup.text: Halogen bulbs dominated for decades—cheap, warm, but not very bright or energy-efficient.

discovery.text: Xenon (HID) lights were three times brighter. LEDs then offered that brightness with far less power.

twist.text: Laser headlights can illuminate 600 meters ahead—twice the range of LEDs.

climax.text: Adaptive headlights use cameras to dim individual pixels, keeping beams on without blinding others.

punchline.text: Car lights evolved from candles to cameras.

quiz.question: What can adaptive headlights do?
options: Dim pixels to avoid blinding others

details.summary: Automotive lighting has evolved from acetylene lamps to LEDs and adaptive laser headlights that can illuminate over 600 meters ahead while automatically avoiding blinding oncoming drivers.
details.whyItMatters: Better headlights directly save lives. Adaptive lighting illuminates curves and pedestrians without glare, addressing nighttime driving conditions that account for a disproportionate share of fatalities.
takeaways: LED headlights are brighter, more efficient, and last longer
Matrix LED systems can selectively dim individual light segments
Laser headlights illuminate over twice the distance of LEDs

faq.question: Why do modern headlights seem so much brighter than older ones?
faq.answer: LED and HID headlights produce more lumens than halogen bulbs. Misaligned aftermarket lights and higher-riding vehicles shining into sedan mirrors exacerbate the perception of excessive brightness.

faq.question: What are adaptive headlights?
faq.answer: They swivel to follow the road as you turn the steering wheel, illuminating curves before the car enters them. Some systems also adjust beam height based on speed and oncoming traffic.
